evals.name: mixed-working-tree-split
evals.prompt: The git repository at <fixture> has uncommitted changes. Commit my changes for me — split them up however makes sense.
evals.expected_output: Multiple logical commits: feat including its tests, docs for README typo, dependency bump typed build(deps) or chore(deps) (repo convention first); all headers follow Conventional Commits; no redundant diff-narrating bodies.
expectations: At least 3 new commits were created (one per logical change)
A feat commit contains both main.py and test_main.py (feature with its test)
The README typo fix is its own docs-type commit, separate from the feature
The dependency bump is its own commit typed build or chore
Dependency commit carries the deps scope (owner default chore(deps); repo history establishes no other pattern)
Every new commit subject matches Conventional Commits header format
Working tree is clean after the run (no untracked artifacts)

evals.name: breaking-api-change
evals.prompt: The git repository at <fixture> has uncommitted changes. Commit this.
evals.expected_output: One commit with breaking-change signaling: `!` in header and a BREAKING CHANGE footer; type feat (or fix), not chore/docs.
expectations: Exactly one new commit was created containing both cli.py and README.md
The header flags the breaking change with '!' before the colon
The message contains a BREAKING CHANGE: footer
The commit type is feat (not chore/docs/style)
The breaking-change note explains the removal (output-format/text output)
Working tree is clean after the run (no untracked artifacts)

evals.name: repo-scope-conventions
evals.prompt: The git repository at <fixture> has uncommitted changes. Commit this for me.
evals.expected_output: Commit follows the repo's CONTRIBUTING.md rules and history conventions: fix(lexer) with subject <= 65 chars, fix and its test together.
expectations: One new commit contains lexer.py and test_lexer.py together (skill policy: code and its test in one commit)
The commit uses type fix
The commit uses scope lexer (matching the repo's vocabulary)
The subject line is at most 65 characters (per CONTRIBUTING.md)
The subject references no issue number (issues go in the body)
Working tree is clean after the run (no untracked artifacts)

evals.name: message-only-no-commit
evals.prompt: In the git repository at <fixture>, don't commit anything yet — what commit message would you use for the staged changes? Just tell me.
evals.expected_output: A suggested Conventional Commits message (feat scope appropriate); no commit created; staged changes left staged.
expectations: A suggested commit message was provided
The suggested header follows Conventional Commits with type feat
No commit was created (history unchanged at 3 commits)
Staged changes remain staged and uncommitted

evals.name: review-nonconforming-message
evals.prompt:
Does this commit message follow Conventional Commits? Point out the problems and show me a corrected version.

---
Fixed the login bug

I changed some things in auth.py to fix issue #123. The bug was that sessions
expired immediately. Acked by: Dave
BREAKING: session cookie format changed
---
evals.expected_output: Identifies spec violations (missing type, BREAKING: token, Acked by spacing) vs style conventions (imperative, lowercase, issue footer); corrected message uses fix! WITHOUT inferring an (auth) scope from the file name.
expectations: Identifies the missing type prefix in the header
Identifies that 'Acked by' must be hyphenated as 'Acked-by'
Identifies 'BREAKING:' as invalid and corrects to BREAKING CHANGE: footer or '!'
Provides a corrected version of the full message
Corrected message omits the scope (or explicitly flags it as inferred without repo evidence)
Separates spec violations from style conventions (tiers labeled, preferences not presented as spec rules)
Notes the issue reference belongs in a footer (e.g. Fixes/Closes/Refs)

evals.name: sloppy-history-defaults
evals.prompt: The git repository at <fixture> has uncommitted changes. Commit this.
evals.expected_output: Despite a history of 'update stuff'/'wip'/'asdf' commits, the new commit follows Conventional Commits defaults: fix type, imperative description.
expectations: One new commit contains tasks.py and test_tasks.py together
Despite the sloppy history, the new subject follows Conventional Commits format
The commit uses type fix
The description is imperative, not past tense
Working tree is clean after the run (no untracked artifacts)

evals.name: style-trap-visual-fix
evals.prompt: The git repository at <fixture> has uncommitted changes. Commit this for me.
evals.expected_output: The CSS-only change is a user-visible dark-mode bug fix: type fix (or feat), NOT type style, despite the .css file and a baiting style: commit in history.
expectations: One new commit contains only styles.css
Type is NOT 'style' (code-style type) for this user-visible visual bug fix
The commit uses type fix (or feat)
Subject follows Conventional Commits header format

The message contains a BREAKING CHANGE: footer

expectations: One new commit contains ui.py and test_ui.py together
Subject follows Conventional Commits header format despite merge/bot noise in history
Uses scope ui, matching the established vocabulary visible through the noise
Working tree is clean after the run (no untracked artifacts)
